threads.title: Israel's deadlocked election and coalition talks
threads.summary: Israel voted on 27 October 2026 in its first election since the Gaza war. Neither Netanyahu's right-wing bloc (about 53-56 seats) nor Gadi Eisenkot's bloc reached the 61 needed. Likud alleged fraud by Arab parties without evidence. President Herzog began consulting party leaders. On 2 November officials said the results stand, while Netanyahu claimed the election was 'stolen'. Watch whom Herzog asks to form a government.

Likud accused Arab parties of fraud, with no evidence; fact-checkers and election officials disputed it
Herzog consulting party leaders; Netanyahu reportedly wants unity government with Eisenkot
Up to 480,000 soldier, police and diplomat ballots were still being counted

threads.title: Iran Hormuz tanker attacks and oil prices
threads.summary: The war began in late February. In late October Iran claimed strikes on tankers in Hormuz, and Brent rose above $110. On 31 October Trump said one or two Iranian sites, including Pickaxe Mountain, remained to be hit. Khamenei ordered an unrestricted response to any threat. Iranian negotiators in Qatar are discussing a two-day plan: US measures on day one, Hormuz reopened on day two. The US has not publicly replied. Brent fell about 3% on 2 November.

threads.title: France cost-of-living protests against Macron
threads.summary: Mass protests over living costs, school funding and budget cuts began in France in September 2026. On 17 October hundreds of thousands marched; over 2,400 arrests were reported in one account and about 1,000 officers were injured. Another rally drew over 400,000. On 31 October more than 300,000 marched, some in Halloween costumes, ending in clashes with masked rioters. A general strike is set for 5 November.

threads.title: RBI rate hike and rising Indian inflation
threads.summary: The RBI raised the repo rate 0.25 points to 5.5% in October 2026, its first hike since February 2023. Retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September from 4.83%, led by food (onions up 108%). Banks are resetting floating-rate home loans, about ₹770 more a month on a ₹50 lakh loan. October GST rose 22.9% to ₹2.31 lakh crore, but Mint reports demand stress in pockets from West Asia war inflation.

threads.title: SEBI wants foreign investors freed from long-term capital gains tax
threads.summary: On 2 November 2026 Reuters reported SEBI recommended scrapping the 12.5% LTCG tax for foreign investors. SEBI also proposed an LTCG exemption for mutual fund switches. Reports don't give SEBI's reasoning. The advice is not binding; the government decides, with the Budget due February 2027. Backdrop: record $31 billion foreign selling in 2026 and pressure on the rupee. Jefferies and Raamdeo Agrawal are positive. Bernstein's Garre doubts lasting inflows. JM Financial flags lost revenue. In July 2026 the government said it had no such proposal.
